AirBubble - version 1.7.2
=========================

File:      AirBubbleSetup.exe (714,248 bytes)
SHA-256:   7221E43D622C2FF9AD30F664CD37B4CBA4812AB78185143213FFC748A43334EA
Signed by: CN=PC Viewer for XREAL glasses (independent build), O=Self-signed
           (self-signed code-signing certificate, thumbprint 9B59D20322D5C17AF5297F692E4B1EB5D6BAFAEF, valid until 2031-11-11)

INSTALL ON ANY PC
  Requirements: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit Intel/AMD (x64); XREAL Air plugged into a USB-C port with video.
  1. Run AirBubbleSetup.exe. One admin prompt installs the virtual screens driver.
     If SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC": click "More info" > "Run anyway".
  2. Plug in the glasses, start "AirBubble", hold still ~2 s the first time.
     It starts with Windows from then on (Startup folder) and shows your screens when the glasses are plugged in.
  Silent install: AirBubbleSetup.exe /S [/desktop] [/noautostart] [/launch] [/nouac]
  Uninstall: Settings > Apps > "AirBubble" (removes the driver it installed too).

ABOUT THE SIGNATURE (please read)
  The app and installer are signed and timestamped with a self-signed certificate, so you can verify they
  haven't been altered (right-click > Properties > Digital Signatures). Windows does not trust self-signed
  certificates by default, so on a new PC it still shows "unknown publisher"/SmartScreen - only a paid
  certificate (or free open-source signing such as SignPath Foundation) removes that everywhere.
  On PCs you own you can make Windows trust it: run Trust-Publisher.cmd once (admin). Undo: Trust-Publisher.cmd remove
  Microsoft Defender scan of the installer, the app and the driver: no threats found.

WHAT'S NEW IN 1.7.2
  - Back to 4 screens by default: 8 made the glasses jittery on integrated graphics.
  - New in Settings: "Allow up to 8 screens (quality may be degraded)". Changing it asks for admin once, restarts
    AirBubble and the virtual screens driver (screens blink and reopen as new screens; Ctrl+Alt+N adds more).
  - Setup keeps whatever you chose there (it raises a smaller pool to 4 but never lowers one you raised to 8).
  Tested on the build PC: 1.7.1 -> 1.7.2 update, then the 8 -> 4 driver change (4 virtual monitors afterwards).
  Not yet tested: ticking/unticking the new checkbox in the Settings window itself.

WHAT'S NEW IN 1.7.1
  - Up to 8 floating screens (was 4). Press Ctrl+Alt+N or "+ New screen" in the dock for each one.
  - Updating from an older version asks for admin once to raise the virtual screens driver from 4 to 8 screens;
    all virtual screens blink while the driver restarts. Screens that were open reopen as new screens once (the
    driver gives them new Windows names), so press Ctrl+Alt+N to bring extra ones back. Your settings stay.
  - Every screen is captured and drawn live: on integrated graphics, many screens playing video at once can get
    choppy. Minimized screens cost almost nothing.
  - Uninstall.exe /setscreens <1-8> (elevated) changes the number of virtual screens of an installed driver.
  Tested: 1.7.0 -> 1.7.1 update on the build PC (driver 4 -> 8 screens, all 8 seen by Windows).

WHAT'S NEW IN 1.7.0
  - New name: "PC Viewer for XREAL glasses" is now AirBubble. The app, Start menu entry, Startup shortcuts,
    installer (AirBubbleSetup.exe), install folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\AirBubble) and settings folder
    (%APPDATA%\AirBubble) all carry the new name.
  - Upgrading from 1.6.x: setup removes the old install (files, shortcuts, Apps entry) and keeps your choices for
    the desktop shortcut and start with Windows. Your settings, API keys, screen layout and Bubble's memory move
    to the new folder the first time AirBubble starts. Tested: 1.6.4 -> 1.7.0 on the build PC.
  - The code-signing certificate is unchanged, so the signature still reads "PC Viewer for XREAL glasses".

WHAT'S NEW IN 1.6.4
  - Easier to pop: a pushed bubble now moves at under half the cursor's speed (at most 7 degrees a second, was
    a bit faster than the cursor), so the cursor always catches up. Once the cursor is over a bubble's middle
    it stops pushing, so you can click it. Bubbles also coast a shorter way after a push.
  Not yet tried in the glasses.

WHAT'S NEW IN 1.6.3
  - Bubbles now appear and hang around the edges of your open screens (a band from a little over the screens'
    edges to a few degrees beyond them) instead of up to 55 degrees off to the side, so they're always within
    easy reach of the cursor. Helpers still appear next to Bubble.
  - A bubble pushed or left far from the screens slowly floats back to within about 10 degrees of them.
  Not yet tried in the glasses.

WHAT'S NEW IN 1.6.2
  - Bubbles now hover gently in one spot instead of roaming around (they still bob and wobble). Move the cursor
    into one and you nudge it along; it glides to a stop and stays there. The push is light: a quick flick of
    the cursor slides right over a bubble, and a still cursor never pushes, so you can always click to pop.
  - New setting, off by default: Settings > Bubble AI > "Free float" - the old behaviour, where bubbles roam
    around your screens and the cursor passes through them.
  Not yet tried in the glasses.

WHAT'S NEW IN 1.6.1
  - Fixed: the AR cursor froze ("mouse broken") whenever an administrator window had the focus, e.g. a terminal
    started as administrator. Windows hides the physical mouse from normal apps in that case, so the real pointer
    moved unseen. The AR cursor now follows the Windows pointer while such a window has the focus, and clicks
    reach that window directly. (AR title bars, the dock and popping bubbles need a normal window in front.)
  - New setting, on by default: Settings > Mouse > "Keep the mouse on the AR screens". The Windows pointer never
    goes onto the PC's own screen or the glasses' display while the glasses are in use. Ctrl+Alt+G still gives
    the mouse back to the normal desktop.
  Not yet tried in the glasses.

WHAT'S NEW IN 1.6.0
  - Bubble can work on his own. Settings > Bubble AI > "Bubble works" (also in the tray menu):
      Ask every time (default) - as before: he asks before each click, typed text, key press and opened app/file.
      Semi-autonomous  - routine steps just happen; he asks before anything large or possibly dangerous
                         (deleting, sending, buying, installing, running programs/scripts/commands, system tools).
      Fully autonomous - he also makes large changes without asking when you asked for them or they clearly follow
                         from what you discussed. He still asks before large or risky things you didn't ask for,
                         and always before commands that could wipe data or weaken the PC. Asks once to turn on.
    Needs "Let Bubble click, type and press keys" for clicking and typing (opening things works without it).
  - Safety net in every mode: the app rates each action itself (what is typed, which keys, what is opened, what is
    clicked and in which window) next to Bubble's own rating, and the stricter one counts. Text on screens and web
    pages never counts as your instructions. He can't click Windows permission prompts or administrator windows.
    After 25 unasked steps in one job he checks in. Say "stop" or pop him to halt a job at once.
  - You see what he does: his card names each action, a ring shows where he clicks, and everything he did, asked
    or was refused is listed in %APPDATA%\XrealPcViewer\bubble_actions.log.
  - He keeps the conversation in mind for longer (old screenshots are dropped instead of the whole chat), so
    "do what we talked about" works.
  - Bubble now talks about "my helpers" or uses their names (Pink, Teal...) rather than describing them by colour.
  - Fixed: a second, small mouse cursor sometimes appeared in one eye. It was the real Windows pointer on the
    glasses' own display. It is now hidden there and moved back under the AR cursor, and the viewer repairs its
    mouse hook if Windows drops it. (While an administrator window has the focus Windows still doesn't let the
    viewer hold the real pointer.)
  Checked on this PC: the app's ratings on 55 sample actions; Bubble in semi and full mode in a dry run (opens
  Notepad unasked, asks before running a script in semi mode, runs it unasked in full mode when asked to, and
  stops to ask what Shift+Delete would hit). Not yet tried with real clicks in the glasses, and the cursor fix
  has not been seen in the glasses yet.

WHAT'S NEW IN 1.5.1
  - Spatial audio: each bubble's voice, pop and "appear" sound come from where it floats (stereo) and stay there
    when you turn your head, even mid-sentence. The far ear hears it slightly later, quieter and duller; behind
    you is duller; nearer is louder. Left/right, front/back and distance only (no up/down cue).
    On/off in Settings > Bubble AI (on by default).
  - The Settings window can be resized and maximized and scrolls when it doesn't fit (it was taller than a
    1080p screen, so the bottom was cut off). Close stays visible at the bottom; the mouse wheel scrolls the
    page instead of changing whichever slider has the focus.
  Checked on this PC: the settings window at several sizes (off-screen render) and the left/right timing and
  loudness of the audio on test signals. Not yet listened to through the glasses.

WHAT'S NEW IN 1.5.0
  - Bubble is an AI buddy: Claude is his brain, ElevenLabs his voice (add your own API keys in Settings >
    Bubble AI; they're stored encrypted for your Windows account and usage is billed to your accounts).
    Say "Bubble" (or press Ctrl+Alt+B) and talk. He answers out loud with a speech card, can look at a screen and
    ring the thing to click, open websites/apps/files, search the web, remember things about you and set reminders.
    App control (click/type/keys) is off by default and asks every time (yes/no, or Ctrl+Alt+Y / N).
  - Conversations: when he asks you something the mic stays open for ~10 s so you can answer without his name;
    otherwise he stays quiet until you call him again.
  - Feelings: his voice shows his mood (laughs, sighs, gasps...) via ElevenLabs' expressive v3 model, and his mood
    carries through the conversation. Being popped doesn't bother him.
  - Helper bubbles: for bigger jobs he sends out up to 4 helpers that work in parallel and report back in their own
    voices. He picks the colours: Pink (bow), Green (sprout), Gold (crown), Purple (wizard hat), Red (horns),
    Orange (propeller beanie), Teal (glasses). Talk to one by its colour; click it to dismiss it.
  - Popping: click a bubble and it pops at once and stops talking. With the AI on, Bubble only comes back when you
    say "Bubble". Bubbles bounce off each other, and overlapping bubbles no longer show square boxes.
  - Privacy: Windows' offline speech recognizer listens for the names; only what you say to a bubble goes to
    ElevenLabs and Claude, and screenshots go to Claude only when he looks at a screen.
  Verified on this PC: questions, web-searching helpers, emotion tags, the wake word and popping in the glasses.

WHAT'S NEW IN 1.4.0
  - Windows permission (UAC) prompts show in the glasses: setup (one admin prompt) turns off Windows' dimmed
    "secure desktop" for UAC, which no app can capture, so the prompt appears on the main AR screen. UAC stays
    on. Settings has a checkbox to switch it back; uninstall restores the previous Windows setting. /nouac skips it.
  - The AR cursor can click UAC prompts and admin windows: over them the real mouse clicks go straight through
    (Windows drops clicks sent by normal apps to more privileged windows).
  - Bubble: a 16-bit pixel-art bubble with a toothy grin floats around near your screens, watches the cursor,
    and pops (with a chiptune "pop") when you click him; a new one floats in a few seconds later.
    On/off in Settings and the tray menu.
  Verified on this PC: Bubble renders in both eyes in 3D and pops on click (self-test readbacks).
WHAT'S NEW IN 1.3.4
  - Starts with Windows by default, from the Startup folder (Win+R, shell:startup): "XREAL PC Viewer" waits in
    the tray and shows your screens when the glasses are plugged in; "XREAL PC Viewer helper" keeps the main
    display right while the viewer isn't showing anything. Untick "Start with Windows" in setup or Settings
    (or delete the shortcut) to turn the viewer's autostart off; silent install: /noautostart.
  - Replaces the registry startup entries of earlier versions (removed on update, so nothing starts twice).
  - The helper now also looks after the desktop while the viewer is waiting in the tray for the glasses.
  Verified on this PC: update from 1.3.3 created both Startup shortcuts, removed the old registry entries,
  and the viewer started straight into AR with the glasses plugged in.

WHAT'S NEW IN 1.3.3
  - 3D calibration (Ctrl+Alt+K, Settings > Calibrate 3D, or the tray menu): a test frame with a red (left eye)
    and green (right eye) line. Up/Down aligns the eyes vertically, Left/Right sets the depth where the two
    images line up (Space = at the main screen), [ ] eye distance; Enter saves, Esc cancels.
  - Edge matching (on by default): the strip at the left/right edge that only one eye can see is faded out, so
    both eyes' images end in the same place and the edges no longer look flat or double.
  Verified on this PC: calibration test pattern lines up in both eyes (readbacks), installed build runs 3D at
  60 fps with the main screen primary, quitting restores laptop primary + glasses Duplicate.

WHAT'S NEW IN 1.3.2
  - The main (primary) display is always somewhere you can see it: the "Main screen" in the glasses while the
    viewer runs; Duplicate (laptop + glasses) when the viewer is closed and the glasses are plugged in; the
    laptop screen alone when they're unplugged. A small background helper (--guard, starts with Windows) handles
    plugging in/unplugging while the viewer is closed. New: --restore-desktop to fix the desktop by hand.
  - 3D (side-by-side) is as smooth as 2D (60 fps; it was ~25 fps because the primary display ended up on the
    laptop screen) and allows multiple screens again (up to 4) - the laptop's output was mistaken for a virtual
    screen after Windows' Duplicate mode had included the virtual screens.
  - Starting the viewer right after plugging in, or right after quitting, waits for the glasses' display
    instead of showing "Couldn't find the glasses".
  Verified on this PC: 2D and 3D at 60 fps with 4 screens, main screen stays primary, desktop restored to
  laptop + glasses Duplicate on quit, installer upgrade restarts the helper.

WHAT'S NEW IN 1.3.1
  - Signed + timestamped app, installer and uninstaller; installer version information.
  - Installer refuses cleanly on unsupported PCs (32-bit or ARM Windows).
  - Uninstall leaves nothing behind (also removes the empty ProgramData folder).
  Verified: full uninstall to a clean state and fresh install from this package.

INCLUDED SINCE 1.3.0
  - Stabilization (head jitter buffer) for chewing/breathing/walking; Off / Light / Medium (default) / Strong.
  - Screen positions and open screens remembered reliably across sessions.
INCLUDED SINCE 1.2.0
  - AR desktop: up to 4 virtual Windows screens that behave like windows (move, push/pull, resize, minimize,
    maximize, lock, close), AR cursor, dock under the main screen, Arrange. PC screen not mirrored.
  - Drift handling (still-period bias learning, temperature-aware, saved; "keep main screen centred").
  - Smooth video (zero-copy capture, paced frames, no mipmap ghosting); side-by-side 3D; start with Windows.

KNOWN LIMITS
  - Tested on the original XREAL Air only (Air 2 / 2 Pro / 2 Ultra recognised but untested).
  - 3DoF: screens hold still when you turn your head, not when you lean.
  - No absolute left/right reference on the Air: very slow drift is absorbed rather than measured.
